Rashi on Gittin 41b:10:1.hebrew: בשטר הוא דפליגי - הדר פריך: נימא בהך מתניתא שטר נקט דוקא, דאילו בכסף, דברי הכל קנה:
Rashi on Gittin 41b:10:1.english: [It is] via a bill [of manumission] that they disagree - [The Gemara] goes back and asks: Let us say [that] in this baraita it specifically cited a bill [of manumission], whereas with money, all agree [that] he acquires [his freedom]:

Rashi on Gittin 41b:10:2.hebrew: נימא תיהוי תיובתא דרב יוסף בתרתי - חדא, דאמר בשטר רבי מודה, והכא תניא דפליג; ועוד, דאמר רב יוסף דבכסף פליגי, וברייתא דיקא דבכסף מודו רבנן דקנה:
Rashi on Gittin 41b:10:2.english: Shall we say that this is a conclusive refutation of Rav Yosef in two [respects] - First, for he said [that] regarding a bill [of manumission] Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] concedes, whereas here it is taught that he disagrees; and furthermore, for Rav Yosef said that they disagree regarding money, whereas the baraita implies that regarding money the Rabbis concede that he acquires [half-freedom]:

Rashi on Gittin 41b:11:1.hebrew: להודיעך כחו דרבי - דאפי' בשטר, דאיכא למגמר "לה לה" מאשה דלא תיפוק לחצאין, פליג:
Rashi on Gittin 41b:11:1.english: To convey to you the strength [of the position] of Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] - that even regarding a bill [of manumission], where one could derive [via the verbal analogy of] "to her, to her" from a [divorced] woman that [she] does not go free by halves, he disagrees:

Rashi on Gittin 41b:12:1.hebrew: להודיעך כחן דרבנן - דאפי' בכסף, דאיכא למדרש "והפדה לא נפדתה", פליגי:
Rashi on Gittin 41b:12:1.english: To convey to you the power of the Rabbis - that even with money, where one can expound "and she has not been redeemed at all," they disagree.

Rashi on Gittin 41b:13:1.hebrew: יכול לכל - שכולה פדויה ונתארסה לעבד עברי קרא משתעי, וקאמר דלא יומתו מחמת ניאוף? תלמוד לומר "לא נפדתה":
Rashi on Gittin 41b:13:1.english: [One] might [think] entirely - [Does] the verse speak [of a case] where she is completely redeemed and betrothed to a Hebrew slave, and [yet] state that they shall not be put to death for adultery? [No, therefore] the verse states, "not redeemed":

Rashi on Gittin 41b:13:2.hebrew: אי לא נפדתה יכול לכל - דלא נפדתה כלל, ואפ"ה מיחייב אשם אביאה דידה, הואיל ונתייחדה לעבד עברי שמותר בשפחה:
Rashi on Gittin 41b:13:2.english: If [it had stated only] “not redeemed,” [one] might [have thought] entirely - [meaning] that she was not redeemed at all, and even so, [one] is liable [for] a guilt offering for relations with her, since she was designated for a Hebrew slave, who is permitted [to cohabit with] a maidservant:

Rashi on Gittin 41b:14:1.hebrew: אין לי אלא בכסף - דאמרי' ביה דנפקא לחירות:
Rashi on Gittin 41b:14:1.english: I have [derived] only via money - [meaning] that we say regarding it that she goes out to freedom:

Rashi on Gittin 41b:14:2.english: Via a bill [of manumission], from where [do we derive] - that she goes out to freedom:

Rashi on Gittin 41b:15:1.hebrew: אין לי אלא חציו בכסף - וכ"ש כולו:
Rashi on Gittin 41b:15:1.english: I have [derived] only half of him via money - and all the more so all of him:

Rashi on Gittin 41b:15:2.hebrew: או כולו בשטר - אבל חציו בשטר עדיין לא למדנו, שאם שיחרר חציו יהא חציו בן חורין:
Rashi on Gittin 41b:15:2.english: Or all of him via a bill [of manumission] - But [regarding] half of him via a bill [of manumission], we have not yet learned that if [the master] emancipated half of him [with a bill], half of him becomes a free man:

Rashi on Gittin 41b:16:1.english: Granted, according to Rav Yosef, after he was refuted - and we established perforce that they disagree in both [cases]:

Rashi on Gittin 41b:16:2.hebrew: הא מני - דאמר דבתרוייהו נפקא לחצאין, רבי היא:
Rashi on Gittin 41b:16:2.english: Whose [opinion] is this - [this baraita] that states that in both [cases] he goes out to half-[freedom] — it is [the opinion of] Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi]:

Rashi on Gittin 41b:16:3.hebrew: אלא לרבה - דאמר בשטר פליגי, אבל בכסף דברי הכל קנה:
Rashi on Gittin 41b:16:3.english: However, according to Rabbah - who said [that] they disagree regarding a document, but regarding money everyone agrees [that] he acquires [himself]:

Rashi on Gittin 41b:16:4.hebrew: רישא - דקתני בכסף לחצאין, דברי הכל:
Rashi on Gittin 41b:16:4.english: The first clause - which teaches [emancipation] with money in halves, [is] everyone's [opinion]:

Rashi on Gittin 41b:16:5.hebrew: וסיפא - דקתני אף בשטר לחצאין, רבי היא ולא רבנן:
Rashi on Gittin 41b:16:5.english: And the last clause - which teaches [that] even with a bill [of manumission he is emancipated] by halves, is [the opinion of] Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] and not [that of] the Rabbis:

Rashi on Gittin 41b:17:1.hebrew: רב אשי אמר רבי היא - רבי אמרה לכולה, דאית ליה בתרוייהו קנה, ורבנן איפלוג עליה בעלמא אשטר ולא אכסף, והא מתניתא מיהא איהו אמרה. ול"ג "ונסיב לה אליבא דתנאי":
Rashi on Gittin 41b:17:1.english: Rav Ashi said: It is [the opinion of] Rabbi - Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] stated all of it [the entire baraita], for he holds regarding both [money and a bill of manumission] that [the slave] acquires [his half-freedom]. And [while] the Rabbis disagreed with him in general regarding a bill [of manumission] and not regarding money, this baraita, at any rate, he [Rabbi] stated it. And we do not have the reading: "and he interprets it according to the Tannaim":

Rashi on Gittin 41b:18:1.english: He establishes it - [meaning] that you find [a case of] a half-slave and half-freeman [through emancipation] with money, and [it is] the opinion of all:

Rashi on Gittin 41b:1:1.english: A free woman he cannot - marry, because of the aspect of slavery in him:

Rashi on Gittin 41b:1:2.hebrew: לא תוהו בראה - יוצר הארץ, לא על תוהו — להיות ריקנית — ברא אותה, כי אם לשבת — להיות בה יישוב — יצרה:
Rashi on Gittin 41b:1:2.english: He did not create it to be a waste - The Creator of the earth did not create it for waste — [meaning] to be empty; rather, [it was] to be inhabited — [meaning] for there to be settlement in it — [that] He formed it:

Rashi on Gittin 41b:2:1.english: He has acquired [himself] - and he becomes half a free man:

Rashi on Gittin 41b:3:1.hebrew: והפדה לא נפדתה - דגבי שפחה חרופה, איכא דדריש ליה בפדויה ואינה פדויה — לקמן ובמסכת כריתות (דף יא.) — חציה שפחה וחציה בת חורין, וסתם פדייה בכסף ובשוה כסף:
Rashi on Gittin 41b:3:1.english: And not at all redeemed - which [is written] regarding a designated maidservant; there are those who expound it as [referring to] one who is redeemed and not redeemed — later [in this tractate] and in Tractate Keritot (11a) — [that is,] half-maidservant and half-freewoman; and an unspecified redemption is with money or with money's worth:

Rashi on Gittin 41b:3:2.hebrew: חופשה לא נתן לה - היינו שטר, דגמר "לה" "לה" מאשה:
Rashi on Gittin 41b:3:2.english: Nor was freedom given to her - This refers to a bill [of manumission], for he derives [a verbal analogy between] "to her" [written here and] "to her" [written regarding] a wife [who is divorced with a bill].

Rashi on Gittin 41b:4:1.hebrew: מה כסף בין כולו בין חציו - כדיליף מ"והפדה לא נפדתה":
Rashi on Gittin 41b:4:1.english: Just as [with] money, either all of him or half of him - as [the Gemara] derives from [the verse], "And she has not been [completely] redeemed" [Leviticus 19:20]:

Rashi on Gittin 41b:5:1.english: Just as [in the case of] a woman, half of her [is] not - A woman is not divorced from her husband in halves:

Rashi on Gittin 41b:6:1.hebrew: רבנן סברי ג"ש עדיף - דלא שבקינן ג"ש וילפינן מהיקש, ורבי סבר היקש עדיף, דכי איכא למילף מהיקש ומג"ש, שבקינן ג"ש וילפינן בהיקש:
Rashi on Gittin 41b:6:1.english: The Rabbis hold [that] a gezerah shavah [verbal analogy] is preferable - for we do not leave aside a gezerah shavah and derive [the law] from a hekkesh [juxtaposition]; and Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] holds [that] a hekkesh is preferable, for when it is possible to derive [the law] from a hekkesh and from a gezerah shavah, we leave aside the gezerah shavah and derive [it] through the hekkesh:

Rashi on Gittin 41b:7:1.hebrew: דכולי עלמא גזירה שוה עדיפא - דכיון דמופנה לדרוש, הוי ליה כמאן דכתביה בגופיה דקרא, דהא קרא יתירא הוא; וכי לאו מופנה נמי, ואין להשיב עליה, כיון דמסיני גמרינן לה — דאין אדם דן ג"ש מעצמו — איהי עדיפא מהיקש:
Rashi on Gittin 41b:7:1.english: Everyone [agrees] a verbal analogy is preferable - For since [the term] is free to be expounded, it is as though it were written in the body of the verse itself, because it is a superfluous verse; and even when it is not free, and there is no refutation against it, since we learn it from Sinai — for a person may not derive a verbal analogy on his own — it is preferable to a juxtaposition:

Rashi on Gittin 41b:7:2.english: For she does not go out with money - therefore she is not divorced in halves:

Rashi on Gittin 41b:7:3.hebrew: תאמר בשפחה שיוצאה בכסף - הלכך, כי נפקא בשטר, תצא אף לחצאין:
Rashi on Gittin 41b:7:3.english: Shall you say [the same] of a maidservant, who goes free through money - Therefore, when she goes free through a document, she goes free even by halves:

Rashi on Gittin 41b:8:1.english: The Torah spoke [in the language of people], etc. - And in fact, [the verse] is speaking of a full [completely unfreed] maidservant:

Rashi on Gittin 41b:8:2.english: [He has] not acquired [himself] - For one derives [the gezerah shavah of] "lah" "lah" ["to her" / "for her"] from a woman [regarding divorce, which cannot take effect partially]:

Tosafot on Gittin 41b:1:1.hebrew: לא תוהו בראה לשבת יצרה - הא דלא נקט קרא ד"פרו ורבו", משום דאי הוה יכול לקיים שבת כל דהו, משום מצות פרו ורבו לא הוה כפינן ליה, והכא כפינן ליה כדפירשנו. אי נמי נקט האי קרא משום דמוכחא דמצוה רבה היא, וכן בפ' בתרא דמגילה (דף כז.) מייתי לה גבי מוכר ספר תורה ללמוד תורה ולישא אשה, דקאמר: שאני תלמוד תורה, דאמר מר: גדול תלמוד תורה כו', אשה נמי "לא תוהו בראה". וה"ר יצחק ברבי מרדכי מפרש דנקט "לשבת יצרה" משום דשייך אף בצד עבדות, אבל פרו ורבו לא שייך אלא בצד חירות. וכן משמע קצת בירושל' דפרקין ודפ"ק דמ"ק, דאמר תמן: תנן, אין נושאין נשים במועד. שמעון בר אבא בשם ר' יוחנן אומר: מפני ביטול פריה ורביה — פירוש: שלא ימתין מלישא עד המועד, שהוא זמן שמחה ופנוי מכלום. בעון קומי רבי אסי: העבד, מהו שישא במועד? אמר להון: נשמענה מן הדא, "יבטל? והלא לא נברא העולם אלא לפריה ורביה". ואמר שמעון בר אבא בשם רבי יוחנן: כל שהוא מצווה על פריה ורביה, אסור לו לישא במועד — פירוש: כל שהוא מצווה על פריה ורביה משום "לשבת יצרה", כגון עבד, אבל אפרו ורבו ודאי לא מיחייב. ולפי זה, בשפחה נמי שייך בה שבת; והא דלא כפינן בחציה שפחה וחציה בת חורין אלא היכא דנהגו בה מנהג הפקר, היינו משום כיון דלא מיפקדא אפרו ורבו, שמא גם לאחר שתשתחרר לא תקיים:
Tosafot on Gittin 41b:1:1.english: He did not create it to be a waste; He formed it to be inhabited - The reason [the Gemara] did not cite the verse "Be fruitful and multiply" is because if he were able to fulfill [the requirement of] "to be inhabited" in any minimal way, we would not force him on account of the commandment of "Be fruitful and multiply," whereas here we do force him, as we explained [earlier]. Alternatively, it cited this verse because it proves that it is a great commandment; and similarly, in the last chapter of Megillah (27a), it brings it regarding one who sells a Torah scroll [only] to study Torah or to marry a woman, where [the Gemara] says: Torah study is different, as the Master said: "Great is Torah study, etc."; [and regarding] a woman as well, [because of] "He did not create it to be a waste." And Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rabbi Mordechai explains that it cited "He formed it to be inhabited" because it applies even to the slave aspect [of him], whereas "Be fruitful and multiply" applies only to the free aspect. And so it is somewhat implied in the Jerusalem Talmud on our chapter and in the first chapter of Moed Katan, where it says there: We learned [in a Mishnah]: One may not marry women on the festival. Shimon bar Abba says in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: Because of the neglect of procreation — meaning, so that one should not wait to marry until the festival, which is a time of joy and free from all [work]. They asked before Rabbi Assi: What is [the law regarding] a slave marrying on the festival? He said to them: Let us learn it from this [Mishnah]: "Should he be idle? But wasn't the world created only for procreation!" And Shimon bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: Anyone who is commanded regarding procreation is forbidden to marry on the festival — meaning, anyone who is commanded regarding procreation on account of "He formed it to be inhabited," such as a slave, though he is certainly not obligated in "Be fruitful and multiply." And according to this, "to be inhabited" applies to a maidservant as well; and the reason we do not force [the master to free] a half-maidservant half-free-woman except where people treat her in a licentious manner is because, since she is not commanded regarding "Be fruitful and multiply," perhaps even after she is freed she will not fulfill [it]:

Tosafot on Gittin 41b:1:2.hebrew: כופין את רבו ועושה אותו בן חורין - וא"ת: וכי אומרים לאדם "חטא כדי שיזכה חבירך", דהכי אמר בפ"ק דשבת (דף ד.) גבי הדביק פת בתנור? וי"ל: דדוקא התם אמרינן הכי, משום דפשע שהדביק סמוך לחשיכה, אבל הכא דלא פשע, לא. וכן בפ' בתרא דערובין (דף קג:) אמר: כהן שעלתה לו יבלת, חברו חותכה לו בשיניו, דקעביד שבות כדי שיזכה חברו בעבודה. וכן בריש תמיד נשחט (פסחים דף נט.) אמר: מחוסר כפרה בערבי פסחים שמביא כפרתו אחר תמיד של בין הערבים, דעשה דפסח שיש בו כרת דחי עשה דהשלמה; אלמא קא עברי כהני בעשה דהשלמה כדי שיזכה זה בפסח! וחציה שפחה וחציה בת חורין דכפו את רבה (לעיל גיטין לח:) משום דנהגו בה מנהג הפקר, אע"ג דהם פושעים, כיון שהיתה מחזרת אחריהם ומשדלתן לזנות, חשיבי כאונסים; ועוד, דמצוה דרבים שאני:
Tosafot on Gittin 41b:1:2.english: His master is forced to make him a freeman - And if you ask: Do we say to a person, "Sin so that your fellow may merit," as [the Gemara] says thus in the first chapter of Shabbat (4a) regarding one who stuck bread in an oven? One can answer: Only there do we say this, because he acted negligently in that he stuck [the bread] close to dark; but here, where he did not act negligently, [we do] not [say this]. And similarly, in the last chapter of Eruvin (103b), [the Gemara] says: A priest on whom a wart grew, his fellow [priest] cuts it off for him with his teeth — for he performs a shevut [rabbinic prohibition] so that his fellow may merit [to participate] in the [Temple] service. And similarly, at the beginning of [the chapter entitled] Tamid Nishchat (Pesachim 59a), [the Gemara] says [that] one who lacks atonement on the eve of Passover brings his atonement [offering] after the afternoon daily offering, because the positive commandment of the Passover [offering], which carries karet [excision], overrides the positive commandment of completion; thus, the priests transgress the positive commandment of completion so that this [person] may merit [to bring] the Passover [offering]! And [as for] the half-maidservant and half-freewoman whose master they forced (above, Gittin 38b) because [people] treated her in a licentious manner — even though they are negligent [sinners], since she was pursuing them and enticing them to engage in harlotry, they are considered like [ones acting under] compulsion; and furthermore, a mitzvah of the many is different:

Tosafot on Gittin 41b:7:1.hebrew: דכ"ע גזירה שוה עדיפא - בריש איזהו מקומן (זבחים דף מח.) ובפ' דם שחיטה (כריתות דף כב:), פליגי ר"ע ורבנן בספק מעילות, ומשמע דלכ"ע הקישא עדיפא; הכא שאני, משום דעיקר שטר מג"ש נפקא לן:
Tosafot on Gittin 41b:7:1.english: Everyone [agrees] that a verbal analogy is preferable - At the beginning of [the chapter entitled] Eizehu Mekoman (Zevachim 48a) and in the chapter [entitled] Dam Shechitah (Keritot 22b), Rabbi Akiva and the Rabbis disagree regarding doubtful cases of me'ilah [misappropriation of consecrated property], and it is implied [there] that according to everyone, a juxtaposition is preferable; [however,] here it is different, because the very [law of] a document [of emancipation] is derived from a verbal analogy:

Tosafot on Gittin 41b:7:2.hebrew: מה לאשה כו' - אע"ג דג"ש מופנה היא, דילפינן מינה מילי טובא, מ"מ כיון דאיכא למיפרך, שבקינן לה משום הקישא:
Tosafot on Gittin 41b:7:2.english: What [is unique] about a woman, etc. - Even though it is a free verbal analogy, from which we derive many things, nevertheless, since it can be refuted, we leave it aside because of the juxtaposition:
